current.text: Andre Drummond has replaced Mitchell Robinson in New York. Towns is a projected starter next to Brunson, Bridges, Hart and Anunoby, and little double-big use is expected.
Without Mitchell Robinson next to him, his rebounds and FG% may go up. His rebounds fell last season while he played next to Robinson.
Coach Mike Brown gives Towns fewer minutes than Thibodeau did, and he plays his bench more instead of overworking the starters.
After the long Finals run, the Knicks are expected to protect his minutes. Over about the first 30 games, they should trim starters' minutes and rest them more on back-to-backs.
One projection has him at only 31 minutes. Experts warn of a championship hangover: a minute or two less per game and a small rise in injury risk.

Experts think his market price is too high. He may take a step back from last season. He is ranked 19th in 9-cat and is not seen as a first-round player. One expert said picks 15 to 17 are too early, and an auction expert valued him at 30-plus USD.
In a recent auction mock draft he went for 36 USD.
The Knicks are projected to win about 50 to 54 games.

durable.text: Rebounds are his clear outlier category, far above the top 250 pool.
He commits many turnovers for a big, which makes TO his weakest category.
He makes more threes than most bigs.
He has a history of lower-body problems, including knee issues.
At age 30 he showed some signs of declining athleticism in the regular season, though he looked good in the playoffs.

note: Our league paid 46 USD for him last season. Yahoo puts his value at 41 USD and ESPN at 37, but the experts value him at 30-plus USD, and in a recent mock he went for 36. Aim for the mid-30s and do not chase him into the 40s. His elite rebounds, good FT% for a big and threes make him a strong fit for punt TO builds. Early in the season, check his minutes during the cautious first 30 or so games and whether his rebounds go up without Mitchell Robinson.
